title: Vocabulary - Core
description: 303 high-frequency SAT words, 87% attested in College Board's own question bank and published practice tests.

cards.back: (adj.) harsh in manner; capable of scratching. His abrasive style cost him allies.
(v.) to decorate. Carved panels adorn the upper gallery.
(adj.) providing a benefit. The site's elevation was advantageous for observing the eclipse.
(n.) a natural liking or close relationship. The dye has a strong affinity for wool but not for cotton.
(adj.) open to more than one interpretation. The ending is deliberately ambiguous, and critics still argue about it.
(adj.) having mixed or contradictory feelings. She was ambivalent about the offer, drawn to the salary but wary of the hours.
(v.) to make better. Terracing ameliorated the worst of the runoff.
(v.) to increase or intensify. Warm water amplifies the storm's intensity.
(adj.) comparable in certain respects. The wing of a bat is analogous to a human hand in its underlying bone structure.
(n.) strong hostility. Old animosity resurfaced during the negotiation.
(v.) to add explanatory notes to. She annotated the margins of every page.
(n.) something that deviates from the norm. The instrument recorded a magnetic anomaly beneath the plain.
(n.) an opponent or adversary. The novel's antagonist is never named.
(n.) something that came before; (adj.) prior. Scholars trace the form to medieval antecedents.
(adj.) directly opposed. Secrecy is antithetical to peer review.
(n.) the act of pacifying by giving in. Critics called the concession pure appeasement.
(v.) to assess the value or quality of. An expert appraised the collection at auction.
(adj.) based on random choice rather than reason. The cutoff at thirty specimens was frankly arbitrary.
(adj.) understood by few; mysterious. The rules of the ceremony are arcane and rarely written down.
(adj.) requiring great effort; difficult. Cataloging the archive was arduous but ultimately rewarding.
(v.) to ease or lessen. Nothing assuaged her doubts about the timeline.
(adj.) not representative of the usual type. The specimen is atypical in both size and color.
(v.) to increase or add to. They augmented the sample with archival records.
(adj.) severely plain; strict. The chapel's austere interior holds nothing but benches.
(adj.) reliable because of expertise; commanding. Her monograph remains the authoritative account.
(adj.) self-governing; independent. Each station operates as an autonomous unit.
(adj.) well-meaning and kind. A benevolent donor funded the whole wing.
(adj.) harmless; kindly. The growth proved benign.
(n.) a flaw or mark; (v.) to spoil. A single blemish on the plate ruined the print.
(v.) to support or strengthen. New evidence bolstered the older interpretation.
(v.) to strengthen or support; (n.) a supporting structure. New satellite images buttress the claim that the glacier is thinning.
(v.) to find a way around; to avoid by cleverness. The design circumvents the need for a cooling fan altogether.
(adj.) logically consistent and clear. The draft is detailed but not yet coherent.
(n.) the state of holding together. Surface cohesion lets the insect stand on water.
(adj.) ordinary, unremarkable; (n.) a trite remark. Once rare, the technique is now commonplace.
(adj.) persuasive; commanding attention. The argument is compelling even where the data thin out.
(adj.) combining so as to complete or enhance. The two studies use complementary methods.
(n.) calm self-control. He kept his composure through a hostile hearing.
(v.) to consist of; to make up. The archive comprises letters, ledgers, and photographs.
(v.) to hide or keep secret. Dense canopy conceals the ruins from aerial photography.
(v.) to admit or grant, often reluctantly. She conceded that the objection had merit.
(v.) to merge two distinct things mistakenly. Critics conflate the author with her narrator.
(v.) to confuse; to defeat expectations. The result confounded everyone's predictions.
(n.) an opinion formed without firm evidence; (v.) to guess. Without the missing volume, the ending is pure conjecture.
(n.) general agreement. A consensus emerged only after three rounds of revision.
(adj.) clearly visible; attracting notice. The absence of citations is conspicuous.
(v.) to restrict or limit. Weight limits constrain what the balloon can carry.
(n.) a limitation or restriction. Budget constraints shortened the survey to one season.
(adj.) causing or marked by disagreement. Water rights remain the most contentious issue in the region.
(adj.) dependent on something else. Funding is contingent on the pilot's success.
(adj.) artificial; obviously planned. The dialogue feels contrived in the closing scene.
(v.) to communicate or transport. The photograph conveys the scale better than any figure.
(adj.) warm and friendly. Relations stayed cordial despite the disagreement.
(v.) to confirm or support with evidence. A second set of ice cores corroborated her estimate of the eruption's date.
(v.) to act against and reduce the effect of. Lime is added to counteract the soil's acidity.
(adj.) believable; worthy of trust. Only one witness gave a credible account.
(v.) to cut short or reduce. Funding cuts curtailed the second phase.
(adj.) distrustful of others' motives. A cynical reading would call the donation a tax maneuver.
(adj.) misleading. The calm surface is deceptive, as the current runs fast beneath.
(adj.) settling an issue; able to decide quickly. The third trial was decisive.
(n.) respectful submission to another's judgment. Out of deference to the family, the letters stayed sealed.
(adj.) no longer existing or functioning. She found the letters in the files of a defunct shipping company.
(v.) to assign responsibility to another; (n.) a representative. She delegated the fieldwork to two graduate students.
(v.) to criticize unfairly; to belittle. It is possible to question the findings without denigrating the researchers.
(v.) to use up or exhaust. Repeated harvests depleted the soil's nitrogen.
(adj.) aimless; lacking purpose or plan. A desultory search of the shelves turned up nothing useful.
(v.) to prescribe or determine authoritatively. Geology, not preference, dictated the route.
(v.) to make or become smaller or less. Repeated exposure diminishes the response.
(v.) to perceive or distinguish, often with effort. It is hard to discern a pattern in so few trials.
(adj.) able to be perceived. There is no discernible difference between the samples.
(adj.) unsettling; causing unease. There was a disconcerting gap between the two clocks.
(n.) an inconsistency between accounts. A small discrepancy in the totals led to the audit.
(n.) good judgment; freedom to decide. Sentencing is left to the discretion of the judge.
(v.) to detach or withdraw. The clutch disengages automatically.
(adj.) not sincere; pretending ignorance. It is disingenuous to call the change minor.
(v.) to belittle or speak of dismissively. Reviewers disparaged the film's score while praising its cinematography.
(adj.) essentially different; not comparable. She drew on disparate fields, from acoustics to zoology.
(adj.) not influenced by emotion; impartial. The report offers a dispassionate account of the failure.
(v.) to scatter or spread out. Seeds disperse on the wind for miles.
(v.) to spread widely. Pamphlets disseminated the findings faster than any journal could.
(v.) to twist out of true shape or meaning. Selective quotation distorts the argument.
(v.) to move or differ apart. The two accounts diverge sharply after the second day.
(adj.) asserting opinions as if unquestionable. His dogmatic insistence on one method alienated collaborators.
(adj.) temporarily inactive. The volcano has been dormant since 1790.
(v.) to shrink gradually. The herd dwindled to fewer than forty animals.
(adj.) sincere and serious. She made an earnest effort to reconcile the accounts.
(n.) effectiveness. The trial measured the vaccine's efficacy in older adults.
(n.) the ability to stretch and recover. The tendon loses elasticity with age.
(v.) to draw out a response. The question elicited a long silence.
(adj.) based on observation or experiment. The claim has strong theoretical appeal but little empirical support.
(v.) to imitate in order to match or surpass. Younger poets emulated her spare line breaks.
(v.) to make into law; to perform. The legislature enacted the measure in spring.
(v.) to include comprehensively. The survey encompasses both banks of the river.
(v.) to publicly support or approve. Two societies endorsed the revised guidelines.
(v.) to last; to withstand hardship. The bridge endured two centuries of flooding.
(v.) to give rise to or cause. The policy engendered more confusion than compliance.
(v.) to involve as a necessary consequence. Restoration entails dismantling the entire roof.
(v.) to establish so firmly as to resist change. The practice became entrenched over generations.
(v.) to be a perfect example of. The chair epitomizes the workshop's spare, functional style.
(adj.) ambiguous; open to two interpretations. His equivocal answer satisfied no one.
(adj.) irregular; unpredictable. The signal was erratic during the storm.
(n.) respect and admiration; (v.) to regard highly. The work is held in high esteem by historians of the period.
(n.) the act of avoiding something. His answer was an elegant evasion.
(v.) to bring to mind. The score evokes the coast without describing it.
(n.) precision; the quality of being exact. The measurements were recorded with unusual exactitude.
(v.) to represent as greater than reality. Early accounts exaggerated the herd's size.
(adj.) complete and thorough, leaving nothing out. Her exhaustive survey cataloged every bird species on the island.
(n.) suitability for a purpose, often over principle. The decision was made from expediency, not conviction.
(adj.) stated clearly and in detail. The instructions are explicit about the order of steps.
(v.) to make full use of, or to use unfairly; (n.) a notable feat. The moss exploits cracks too narrow for other plants.
(v.) to praise highly. Early reviewers extolled the novel's structure.
(adj.) irrelevant; not belonging. Trim the extraneous detail from the opening paragraph.
(v.) to extend known data to estimate the unknown. It is risky to extrapolate from three data points.
(adj.) easy in a superficial or glib way. The comparison is facile and collapses on inspection.
(v.) to make easier. A shared glossary facilitated the collaboration.
(adj.) possible and practical to do. Tunneling proved feasible only on the eastern slope.
(v.) to prevent by acting first. Early irrigation forestalled the worst of the drought.
(v.) to predict. Ring width in these pines foretells nothing about the coming year.
(v.) to encourage or promote growth. The program fosters collaboration between the two departments.
(adj.) easily broken or damaged. Hollow construction left the sculpture especially fragile.
(adj.) deceitful; obtained by deception. Several fraudulent specimens entered the collection.
(adj.) producing no result. Three fruitless days of dredging yielded nothing.
(v.) to hinder or impede. Thick ice hampered the survey for weeks.
(adj.) lacking order or plan; random. Specimens had been stored in haphazard fashion, with no labels or dates.
(v.) to obstruct or delay. Loose scree hindered the descent.
(v.) to accumulate and hide away; (n.) a hidden store. Jays hoard far more acorns than they retrieve.
(adj.) uniform in composition. The sample looked homogeneous but contained three distinct minerals.
(v.) to propose an explanation for testing. They hypothesized that light, not heat, triggers the bloom.
(adj.) peculiar to an individual. Her spelling is idiosyncratic but consistent.
(adj.) forbidden by law or custom. The illicit trade in orchids continues.
(v.) to give or communicate. Oak barrels impart a faint vanilla note.
(adj.) unbiased; treating all sides equally. An impartial panel reviewed every appeal.
(v.) to slow or obstruct. Silt impedes the flow through the narrower channels.
(adj.) about to happen, often something unwelcome. Sudden brightening of the corona signals an impending flare.
(adj.) essential; urgent. Rapid cooling is imperative at this stage.
(adj.) too slight to be noticed. The drift is imperceptible over a single season.
(adj.) implied rather than directly stated. The essay carries an implicit criticism of its own methods.
(adj.) not sensible or workable in reality. Shipping the stone intact proved impractical.
(adj.) unintentional; accidental. An inadvertent keystroke deleted the afternoon's measurements.
(adj.) not leading to a firm result. Two trials were inconclusive and a third was never run.
(adj.) out of place; inconsistent with its surroundings. The glass tower looked incongruous among the low brick storefronts.
(adj.) unimportant. The discrepancy is real but inconsequential.
(adj.) impossible to read or understand. Centuries of water damage left the lower half of the tablet indecipherable.
(adj.) impossible to question or deny. The fossil record on this point is indisputable.
(v.) to bring about; to persuade. Low temperatures induce dormancy in the seeds.
(v.) to yield to a desire; to allow oneself. He indulged a long-standing interest in maps.
(adj.) failing to produce the intended effect. The ban proved ineffectual because it was never enforced.
(n.) resistance to change or motion. Institutional inertia delayed the reform for a decade.
(adj.) certain to happen; unavoidable. Some loss of detail is inevitable at this resolution.
(adj.) impossible to explain. The gap in the record remains inexplicable.
(adj.) incapable of being wrong. No instrument is infallible, and this one drifts with heat.
(adj.) harmless; unlikely to offend. What sounded like an innocuous question turned out to be the heart of the interview.
(adj.) featuring new methods or ideas. Her innovative use of mirrors doubled the light.
(adj.) impossible to overcome. The obstacles looked insurmountable until the route was resurveyed.
(adj.) unable to be touched; hard to define. Reputation is an intangible but decisive asset.
(adj.) essential to the whole. Improvisation is integral to the form, not an ornament added to it.
(adj.) able to be swapped without difference. The terms are not quite interchangeable.
(adj.) mutually reliant. The two species are wholly interdependent.
(v.) to insert a remark. He interjected a correction before she could finish.
(adj.) very detailed and complicated. The beetle's shell has an intricate lattice that scatters light.
(v.) to make void or prove wrong. A single contaminated sample invalidated the run.
(adj.) impossible to harm. No system is invulnerable to a determined attacker.
(adj.) not connected to the matter at hand. The author's nationality is irrelevant to the claim.
(adj.) showing good judgment. A judicious edit cut the chapter in half.
(v.) to place side by side for contrast. The exhibit juxtaposes the two portraits.
(adj.) using very few words. His laconic reply ended the discussion.
(adj.) present but not yet visible or active. The virus can stay latent for years.
(adj.) valid, lawful, or justifiable. That is a legitimate objection and deserves an answer.
(adj.) clear and easy to understand. The book is a lucid introduction to a difficult field.
(adj.) producing great profit. Dye extraction became a lucrative trade in the port cities.
(adj.) required by rule. Reporting became mandatory in 1998.
(v.) to show plainly; (adj.) obvious. The disorder manifests differently in adults.
(v.) to push to the edge of importance. The debate marginalized the very communities it concerned.
(adj.) extremely careful about detail. Her meticulous records made the reanalysis possible.
(v.) to imitate closely. The orchid mimics a female wasp to attract pollinators.
(adj.) disliking humankind. His misanthropic reputation was undeserved and largely self-authored.
(v.) to misinterpret. Brevity in an email is easily misconstrued as coldness.
(n.) a feeling of doubt or unease. She signed the contract despite serious misgivings.
(v.) to make less severe. Planting along the banks mitigates erosion during floods.
(adj.) vague; ill-defined. The plan remained nebulous well into spring.
(v.) to nullify or contradict. Heat loss negates most of the efficiency gain.
(adj.) so small as to be unimportant. The added weight had a negligible effect on fuel use.
(adj.) existing only as an idea; hypothetical. The deadline was notional from the start.
(adj.) new and unusual. The team proposed a novel method for storing hydrogen at low pressure.
(n.) a subtle difference in meaning or tone. The translation captures the plot but loses the nuance of the original.
(v.) to make legally void or ineffective. The court nullified the earlier ruling.
(v.) to hide or make unclear; (adj.) little known. Dense fog obscured the summit until late afternoon.
(adj.) quick to notice things. An observant assistant caught the mislabeled jar.
(adj.) no longer in use. The format became obsolete within a decade.
(v.) to make unnecessary. The new seal obviates the need for annual maintenance.
(adj.) casual, done without preparation. An offhand remark became the paper's title.
(adj.) not transparent; hard to understand. The regulation's opaque wording left even lawyers uncertain.
(v.) to make as effective as possible. They optimized the array for low-light conditions.
(adj.) decorative rather than functional. The ironwork is purely ornamental.
(adj.) apparent but perhaps not genuine. The ostensible reason was cost.
(adj.) frank in stating opinions. She was an outspoken critic of the plan.
(v.) to surpass or exceed. Demand quickly outstripped the mill's capacity.
(v.) to fail to notice; to disregard. Earlier surveys overlooked the smaller of the two moons.
(adj.) done openly, not concealed. There was no overt hostility, only a long and telling silence.
(n.) a model or typical pattern of thought. The finding forced a shift in the prevailing paradigm.
(n.) a seemingly self-contradictory truth. The paradox is that adding lanes can slow traffic.
(v.) to become aware of; to interpret. Bees perceive ultraviolet patterns invisible to us.
(adj.) able to be noticed. There is a perceptible warming trend in the record.
(adj.) of minor importance; on the edge. Costs were treated as a peripheral concern until the final review.
(adj.) never ending; continuous. The mill ran on the perpetual current of the river.
(adj.) continuing firmly despite difficulty. A persistent drizzle ruined the exposure.
(adj.) spreading widely throughout. The smell of tar was pervasive.
(adj.) seeming reasonable or probable. The simplest explanation is also the most plausible.
(adj.) practical rather than idealistic. His pragmatic approach traded elegance for something that would ship on time.
(adj.) unstable; dangerously uncertain. The nest sits in a precarious fork near the crown.
(v.) to cause to happen suddenly; (adj.) hasty. The frost precipitated an early harvest.
(v.) to prevent or make impossible. Poor weather precluded any flying that week.
(n.) something that comes before and leads to. This alloy was a precursor to modern steel.
(v.) to foreshadow. The early sketches prefigure the mural's final composition.
(adj.) planned in advance. The remark was clearly premeditated.
(n.) widespread respect and high standing. The prize carries more prestige than money.
(v.) to assume in advance. The question presupposes that the practice was voluntary.
(adj.) attempting to impress by affecting importance. The menu's pretentious language obscured simple food.
(v.) to prove more powerful; to be widespread. Westerly winds prevail in late autumn.
(adj.) competent and skilled. She became proficient in three scripts.
(adj.) very deep or intense; showing great insight. The discovery had profound consequences for the field.
(v.) to increase rapidly in number. Algae proliferate in the warmer shallows.
(adj.) producing much. She was a prolific correspondent.
(v.) to extend in duration. Cold storage prolongs the shelf life considerably.
(n.) a natural tendency. The alloy has a propensity to crack under cold.
(adj.) drawn out; lasting longer than expected. A protracted dispute stalled the excavation.
(adj.) showing careful, sensible judgment. It seemed prudent to test the prototype before announcing a launch date.
(v.) to express as a measurable amount. Losses of this kind are hard to quantify.
(adj.) stubbornly resisting authority or control. The recalcitrant senator refused to back any version of the bill.
(v.) to formally withdraw a previous statement. Under pressure he recanted his testimony.
(v.) to respond to an action in kind. The gesture was never reciprocated.
(n.) mutual exchange for mutual benefit. The treaty rests on reciprocity rather than enforcement.
(v.) to make consistent; to restore friendly relations. It is hard to reconcile the two accounts.
(v.) to correct or put right. The agency moved quickly to rectify the error in the published tables.
(adj.) unnecessary because already present. The third sensor is redundant but guards against failure.
(v.) to prove false or disprove. A single reproducible experiment refuted decades of assumption.
(v.) to say again for emphasis. She reiterated that the data were preliminary.
(v.) to assign to a lower position. The findings were relegated to an appendix.
(adj.) able to be reproduced. A result is worthless unless it is replicable.
(n.) a temporary relief or delay. Rain gave the crews a brief reprieve from the heat.
(v.) to reject or disown. The author later repudiated the theories of her first book.
(adj.) able to recover quickly from difficulty. Mangrove forests are surprisingly resilient after storm surges.
(adj.) controlled; not excessive. The prose is restrained where the subject invites melodrama.
(v.) to keep or hold onto. Clay soils retain water far longer than sand.
(adj.) looking back on the past. A retrospective review found the same error in earlier volumes.
(n.) deep respect. The site is treated with reverence by both communities.
(adj.) strong and resistant to failure. The conclusion is robust across every model.
(adj.) basic; undeveloped. The early model had only rudimentary steering.
(adj.) cheerfully optimistic. Despite the setback he remained sanguine about the project's chances.
(v.) to examine closely and critically. Reviewers scrutinized every figure in the appendix.
(adj.) showing sharp practical judgment. A shrewd reading of the market saved the firm.
(adj.) exceptional; unique. She had a singular gift for explaining hard ideas.
(adj.) not easily convinced; doubting. Reviewers were skeptical of so large an effect.
(adj.) highly developed or complex; refined. The clock uses a surprisingly sophisticated escapement.
(v.) to form a theory without firm evidence. We can only speculate about the builder's intent.
(adj.) false; not genuine. The correlation turned out to be spurious.
(adj.) requiring great exertion. The ascent is strenuous but requires no technical gear.
(v.) to block or thwart. Persistent rain stymied every attempt to finish the excavation.
(adj.) lower in rank; (v.) to treat as less important. Style is subordinate to clarity here.
(v.) to back up a claim with proof. The lab could not substantiate the company's advertised battery life.
(adj.) delicate; not obvious. A subtle shift in the vowel marks the speaker's region.
(adj.) seeking to undermine an established system. The pamphlets were considered subversive and suppressed.
(adj.) briefly and clearly expressed. Her succinct summary ran to four sentences.
(v.) to yield or give way to. Most seedlings succumb to frost in the first week.
(adj.) shallow; concerned only with the surface. Her knowledge of the topic proved superficial under questioning.
(adj.) more than is needed. The final paragraph is superfluous.
(v.) to replace something older. The 1911 edition supersedes all earlier printings.
(v.) to add to; (n.) an addition. Field notes supplement the photographic record.
(n.) an assumption or belief held without proof. The argument rests on the supposition that prices stay flat.
(v.) to hold back, restrain, or prevent. The drug suppresses the immune response that causes the swelling.
(v.) to guess from limited evidence. From the wear on the steps he surmised the door saw daily use.
(adj.) done secretly. A surreptitious glance at her notes gave away the answer.
(n.) a brief summary. The catalog gives a one-paragraph synopsis of each play.
(adj.) understood without being stated. There was a tacit agreement not to raise it.
(adj.) only slightly relevant. The footnote raises a tangential point about printing costs.
(adj.) perceptible by touch; concrete. The program produced tangible improvements.
(adj.) tiresome because long or dull. Copying the ledgers was tedious but necessary.
(adj.) weak, thin, or flimsy. The link between the two events rests on tenuous circumstantial evidence.
(adj.) brief and to the point, sometimes curtly. His terse note said only that the meeting was off.
(adj.) calm and peaceful. The bay is tranquil in the hour before dawn.
(v.) to go beyond the limits of. The best of these songs transcend their genre.
(adj.) lasting only briefly. The effect is transient and fades within hours.
(adj.) present everywhere. Plastic fibers are now ubiquitous in river sediment.
(adj.) unable to be attacked or questioned. Her command of the sources is unassailable.
(adj.) modest; not seeking attention. The unassuming building houses one of the finest collections in Europe.
(adj.) free from prejudice. Randomizing the order produced an unbiased sample.
(adj.) unable to be disputed. The improvement in air quality is undeniable.
(v.) to judge as smaller or less capable than reality. Early models underestimated the rate of melt.
(v.) to weaken gradually. Leaks undermined the foundation over decades.
(v.) to emphasize. The outbreak underscores the need for surveillance.
(adj.) not noticeable; inconspicuous. Sensors were placed in unobtrusive housings along the trail.
(adj.) derivative; lacking novelty. The melody is pleasant but unoriginal.
(adj.) never done or known before. The melt rate is unprecedented in the record.
(adj.) ordinary; not worth noting. The exterior is unremarkable, but the interior is extraordinary.
(adj.) constant; never changing. The cave maintains an unvarying temperature year round.
(adj.) not clearly expressed or defined. The brief was too vague to act on.
(v.) to confirm the accuracy or legitimacy of. Independent researchers validated the model against forty years of data.
(adj.) genuine; used for emphasis. The estuary is a veritable nursery for young fish.
(adj.) capable of working or surviving. Only one of the proposals is financially viable.
(n.) watchful attentiveness. Constant vigilance kept the levees intact.
(v.) to clear of blame; to justify. Later measurements vindicated her estimate.
(adj.) unstable; liable to change suddenly. Prices stayed volatile through the winter.
(v.) to give up a right or requirement. The journal waived the fee for student authors.
